speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To help me understand what is happening, can you tell me if you have been vomiting, and if so, does the vomit ever look like it contains bile or looks like coffee grounds?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Electrolytes, Liver_Function_Tests, Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the results; since your blood work and initial ultrasound are normal, I need to know if you have been passing stool regularly or if your abdomen feels tight and hard to the touch. Have you noticed any visible peristalsis (wavelike movements) across your belly, or does your rectum feel empty when checked?

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception. Please confirm if you have noticed episodes of "currant jelly" stool (blood and mucus mixed) or if the baby has had periods of being very quiet and pale followed by sudden, severe crying episodes.

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray (to look for a "target sign" or pneumoperitoneum confirming obstruction or perforation).
